classification.habit: Perennial semi-aquatic, aromatic herb with a creeping branched rhizome and sword-shaped leaves.
classification.habitat: Marshy places, banks of streams, ponds and wet fields.
classification.distribution: Throughout India up to about 2,200 m in the Himalaya, especially Manipur, Nagaland and the North-East; widely cultivated.

identification.description: Sub-cylindrical tortuous branched rhizomes marked with triangular leaf scars and rootlets, brownish exterior and whitish spongy interior, strong peculiar aromatic odor and warm pungent bitter taste.
identification.whole_plant: Iris-like marsh herb with a stout, aromatic, horizontally creeping rhizome and tufts of erect sword-shaped leaves.
identification.root: Numerous fibrous roots arise from the lower side of the rhizome, leaving tubercular root scars.
identification.stem: Rhizome sub-cylindrical to slightly flattened, 0.5–1.5 cm thick, tortuous; upper side with alternate triangular leaf scars almost encircling it, lower side with tubercular root scars; light brown with reddish tinge outside, buff inside; fracture short; aromatic, pungent and bitter (API).
identification.leaf: Ensiform (sword-shaped) leaves up to about 1 m long with a prominent midrib and wavy margin, aromatic when crushed.
identification.flower: Minute yellowish-green flowers packed on a cylindrical spadix 5–10 cm long, borne laterally on a leaf-like scape.
identification.fruit: Small berries; rarely formed in India.
identification_points: Sub-cylindrical tortuous branched rhizomes marked with triangular leaf scars and rootlets, brownish exterior and whitish spongy interior, strong peculiar aromatic odor and warm pungent bitter taste.

therapeutics.dose: Churna 60–120 mg (API; after shodhana only); 1–2 g for vamana
therapeutics.anupana: Madhu (honey) or Ksheera (milk) for Medhya use
therapeutics.precautions: Ushna-Tikshna drug with emetic action in larger doses: use only in prescribed dose and preferably after shodhana. Avoid long-term or high-dose use; the β-asarone content of tetraploid (Indian) chemotypes is a safety concern. Use cautiously in Pitta disorders.
therapeutics.contraindications: Pregnancy and lactation, Raktapitta and bleeding states, Pitta-predominant conditions, and young children except in small classical doses under supervision.

shlokas:
वचोग्रगन्धा कटुका तिक्तोष्णा वान्तिवह्निकृत् ।
विबन्धाध्मानशूलघ्नी शकृन्मूत्रविशोधिनी ॥
अपस्मारकफोन्मादभूतजन्त्वनिलान् हरेत् ॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The rhizome contains a volatile oil rich in asarones (especially β-asarone in Indian strains) plus the bitter glucoside acorin (API).

modern_information.evidence_summary: Sweet flag is a powerful herb for the mind, improving speech, intelligence, and clearing toxins from the nervous system.
recognized_uses: Nervine, memory and speech in traditional practice
modern_information.safety_notes: β-Asarone has shown toxicity and carcinogenicity in animal studies; oral use should be short-term, in low doses and on professional advice.
